title: Krishna's Peace Mission and the Five Villages
text:
After their thirteen years of exile, the five Pandava brothers asked their cousin Duryodhana to return the half of the kingdom that had been taken from them in a rigged game of dice. Duryodhana refused. War between the two branches of the family seemed certain.

The eldest Pandava, Yudhishthira, made one last offer to avoid bloodshed. He would give up the claim to half the kingdom and accept just five villages, one for each brother. Krishna himself traveled to the Kaurava court at Hastinapura as envoy to plead for peace. The elders of the court, Bhishma, Drona and Duryodhana's own father, the blind king Dhritarashtra, all urged Duryodhana to accept.

Duryodhana would not. He declared that he would not give the Pandavas even as much land as could be pierced by the point of a needle. He even tried to have Krishna seized, and Krishna revealed his divine form to the court before he left.

The war that followed on the field of Kurukshetra lasted eighteen days. Almost every warrior on both sides was killed, including Duryodhana and all his brothers.
lesson: When the other side asks for very little, refusing out of pride can cost you everything. Know what you can afford to give before a dispute becomes a fight no one wins.
people: Krishna, Duryodhana, Yudhishthira, the Pandavas, Dhritarashtra
